paragraphs: Here's what David teaches us, baker: when your heart is faint, you don't have to fix yourself first. David cries out and asks, "Lead me to the rock that is higher than I." (Psalm 61:2) I think that's the whole point. He doesn't map out the route himself, he asks God to lead him to the rock.

Look at his reason, too. He says, "For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy." (Psalm 61:3) David doesn't ask because he hopes God might show up. He asks because he already knows what God has been to him. Then he asks to dwell in God's tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of His wings (Psalm 61:4), and friend, that's a request for a home, not a quick visit.

And notice where the psalm ends up. David says God has given him "the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name," (Psalm 61:5) the prayer asks for God's "loving devotion and Your faithfulness" to guard the king (Psalm 61:7), and David closes with a promise to sing praise and fulfill his vows day by day (Psalm 61:8). So the next time your heart goes faint, baker, call out. Run to the Rock that is higher than you, and then sing about it day after day.
